author: Staff Reports
title: State election training quiet despite national debate - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Reports ,
5 hours ago Blount County Administrator of Elections Moe Click and members of his staff joined more than 350 county election officials from across Tennessee on Monday for the Tennessee Division of Elections’ Election Seminar as they prepare for the Aug. 6 primary and general election.
“It was another great turnout for the annual Tennessee Division of Elections statewide training seminar. I am proud of the hard work and dedication of our election officials statewide,” said Secretary Hargett “These Tennesseans help make our state a place where it is easy to vote, but hard to cheat.”
The seminar featured presentations on constitutional amendments and new election laws, disaster preparedness, election commission duties, voter list maintenance, campaign finance, and civic engagement. County election officials also received updates from the United States Postal Service.
“Our election officials are the best in the nation because they are committed to hard work, continuous training, and professional development,” said Coordinator of Elections Mark Goins. “Their dedication is one of the many reasons Tennessee has been recognized as the nation’s leader in election integrity for five consecutive years.”
The Election Seminar provides county election officials with the information and resources to administer elections consistently and in accordance with Tennessee law.
Click confirmed for The Daily Times that while voting identification and Supreme Court rulings on election law have dominated national headlines over the past week, little of that was brought up at the conference as Tennessee already requires nearly every portion of what’s required in the current version of the Save America Act.
DEADLINE: The deadline for new voter registration for the Aug. 6 election is Tuesday, July 7.
UP NEXT: The Election Commission will meet again at 11 a.m. Wednesday, July 15 at the courthouse.
